sections.heading: India's energy profile — needs and arithmetic

blocks.text: India is the **world's third-largest energy consumer** (after China & the US) yet runs on roughly **one-third of the global per-capita average** — the headroom that makes India **the largest source of future energy-demand growth** (IEA: ~25% of global demand growth to 2040). The mix (primary energy): **coal ~55%, oil ~26%, gas ~6%, renewables+hydro ~7-8%, nuclear ~1-2%**; electricity capacity ~**485+ GW (2025)** with **non-fossil ~50% of capacity** (achieved ahead of the 2030 NDC) but fossil still ~75% of **generation** — the capacity-vs-generation distinction every answer needs. Import exposure: **~88% of crude, ~50% of gas, even coking coal** — the security core (E2-016).

rows: Created **BEE**; 2022 amendments: **carbon-credit trading scheme (CCTS)**, non-fossil purchase obligations, large buildings in code
Energy-intensity targets for designated consumers with tradable ESCerts — multiple cycles, ~2% intensity gains per cycle band
**UJALA (~37 crore LEDs)**, Street-lighting programme, **ECBC/Eco Niwas** codes
LED price crash (₹310→₹38 era) — the world-cited procurement success
PM-KUSUM solar pumps; FAME-II/PM E-DRIVE EV push; fuel-economy (CAFE) norms

blocks.text: **Resource endowment**: coal reserves ~350+ bn tonnes (5th largest; quality caveat — high ash), lignite (Neyveli belt), modest oil (Bombay High, Rajasthan), gas (KG basin — **AP's offshore relevance**), hydro potential ~145 GW (half tapped), solar ~750 GW potential, wind ~1,160 GW (at 150 m), **thorium's world-class monazite beach sands (AP-Odisha-TN coasts)** — the endowment sentence that links straight to AP.

items: **How much?** Demand doubles-plus by 2047 (electricity faster — cooling, EVs, data centres as the new demand trio); peak demand crossed **250 GW (2024)** — plan for the peak, not the average.

**From what?** The transition is **additive, not substitutive** in the near term: renewables take growth's share while coal holds the base — the '**coal plateau, clean growth**' honest description; efficiency is the 'first fuel' (cheapest MW is the one not needed — PAT/UJALA's case).

**Delivered how?** The grid's stress points: DISCOM finances (AT&C ~15%+, RDSS's metering fix), storage scarcity (PSP+BESS pipeline), transmission for RE zones — delivery, not generation, is the binding constraint.

**AP hook**: energy-intensity leadership (AP among top EE-implementing states — LED streetlighting first-mover), KG-gas landfall, the PSP pipeline (~40 GW identified) and solar parks — the state as the transition's test bed (full AP file in PIV-IDA-045/IA-051).

blocks.text: Exam tip: Open with the paradox — 'third-largest consumer, one-third per-capita' — and close with delivery-as-the-binding-constraint. The examiner sees a thousand lists of schemes; the four-question frame is what distinguishes.

prelimsPointers: India: **3rd-largest energy consumer**; per-capita ~**one-third of world average**; largest future demand-growth source (IEA).
**EC Act 2001 → BEE (2002)**; **2022 amendment** enabled the **carbon-credit trading scheme (CCTS)**.
**PAT scheme**: energy-intensity targets + tradable **ESCerts** for designated consumers.
**UJALA**: ~37 crore LED bulbs; LED procurement price fell ~90% — the demand-aggregation classic.
Installed capacity ~**485 GW (2025)**; **non-fossil ≈50% of capacity** achieved 2025 (ahead of NDC 2030); peak demand crossed **250 GW (May 2024)**.
Crude import dependence ~**88%**; gas ~50%; coal reserves ~**350+ billion tonnes** (high-ash).
**Monazite (thorium) beach sands** concentrate on AP-Odisha-Kerala-TN coasts — India's three-stage programme's endowment.
**ECBC/Eco Niwas Samhita** — commercial/residential building energy codes.
mainsAngles: Third-largest consumer at one-third per-capita — decode India's energy arithmetic and its 2047 implications.

Delivery, not generation, binds India's energy future — argue with DISCOM, storage and grid evidence.
Audit India's resource endowment from high-ash coal to thorium sands, and the strategy each dictates.

sections.heading: Policy & programme stack — and its evaluation

items: **Targets**: NDC 2030 — 50% non-fossil capacity (met early), 45% emission-intensity cut; **500 GW non-fossil by 2030** (the political target; ~last-100-GW challenge); Net Zero 2070.

**Programme stack**: National Solar Mission (2010's 20 GW dream → 100+ GW reality), **PLI for modules & ALMM** (import substitution vs cost tension), **PM-KUSUM** (farm solar's three components), **PM Surya Ghar** (rooftop democratisation), **Green Energy Corridors** (transmission), **RE bidding trajectory (50 GW/yr)**, **Offshore wind VGF**, **National Green Hydrogen Mission**, **BESS VGF (2023-)** and the **CCTS carbon market** — the complete acronym armoury with one line each.

**Evaluation ledger**: costs collapsed (solar's ~₹2.5), capacity soared — but **integration debts** (curtailment risk, storage shortfall, DISCOM must-run stress), **land-and-transmission frictions**, **rooftop-and-agri lag** vs utility success, **China-dependence** in cells-wafers (PLI's slow onshoring), and the **AP PPA-renegotiation episode (2019)** as the sanctity-of-contract cautionary tale — celebrate + audit in the same paragraph.

**AP anchor**: solar parks (Kurnool 1,000 MW; NP Kunta), Rayalaseema wind, **Pinnapuram integrated RE-storage (world-scale)**, green-hydrogen MoUs (~₹2 lakh crore era announcements), rooftop's coastal potential — AP as the storage-backed-renewables laboratory.

blocks.text: Exam tip: The examiner's discriminator is the integration paragraph — storage, transmission, DISCOM economics. Capacity numbers impress; the delivery-system understanding scores.

prelimsPointers: Solar ~**110+ GW**, wind ~**50 GW**, total RE (incl. large hydro) ~**220+ GW** within ~485 GW (2025).
**PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (2024)**: 1 crore rooftop-solar homes; up to 300 free units logic; ~₹75,021 crore.
**National Green Hydrogen Mission (Jan 2023)**: ₹19,744 crore; **5 MMT/yr by 2030**; SIGHT incentives; **NTPC Pudimadaka (Vizag)** among the first hubs.
**PM-KUSUM**: components A (small RE plants), B (standalone pumps), C (feeder/pump solarisation).
**E20 petrol achieved by 2025** (target preponed from 2030); SATAT for compressed biogas.
**Offshore wind**: ~37 GW potential zones off Gujarat & TN; VGF scheme approved 2024 (1 GW initial).
**BESS VGF (2023)** and **PSP guidelines** — the storage push; AP's PSP pipeline ~**40 GW** identified.
**ALMM** (approved models & manufacturers list) + module **PLI** — solar supply-chain onshoring instruments.

sections.heading: Conventional vs non-conventional — the comparison core

rows: **Dispatchable** — follows load (coal's ramping limits aside); the grid's inertia and base
Capex-heavy, near-zero marginal cost — tariff certainty once built
CO2 (~0.9-1 kg/kWh coal), PM-SOx-NOx, ash ponds, mining displacement
Minimal operating emissions; land-use, mineral supply chains, end-of-life waste
Large central stations, anywhere fuel reaches
Resource-tied (sun-wind-tide maps decide); modular — rooftop to park
Coal ~210+ GW capacity, ~75% generation; gas underused (~25 GW at low PLF); large hydro ~47 GW
Solar 110+, wind ~50, bio ~11 GW; geothermal-tidal at pilot stage

blocks.text: *Large hydro straddles the line — renewable by flow, 'conventional' by vintage and scale; since 2019 India counts it renewable: a favourite prelims nuance.

sections.heading: The five non-conventional files — one paragraph each

items: **Solar**: PV (crystalline dominant; thin-film niche) + CSP (Rajasthan pilots); resource ~4-7 kWh/m²/day nationally; India's cost revolution (E2-014); **floating solar** (Ramagundam 100 MW; reservoir synergy — evaporation cut + no land) and **agrivoltaics** as land-answers.

**Wind**: kinetic energy ∝ v³ — siting is everything (passes of TN/AP's Rayalaseema, Gujarat coast); hub heights rising (120-150 m unlocking 1,160 GW potential); hybrid (wind+solar+BESS) parks the new tender norm.

**Bio-energy**: combustion-cogeneration (bagasse), biomethanation (CBG), liquid fuels (1G molasses-ethanol → **2G ligno-cellulosic** — Panipat; used-cooking-oil biodiesel); carbon-neutral in principle, collection-economics-bound in practice; stubble-to-energy as the air-quality twofer.
**Geothermal**: India's ~10 GW-scale theoretical niche — **Puga (Ladakh) pilot**, Tattapani, Manikaran springs; direct-use (space heating, drying) more viable than power near-term.

**Tidal & ocean**: Gulf of **Khambhat/Kutch** (~12,500 MW theoretical) and Sundarbans creeks; high capex + ecology stalled projects; **OTEC** (Kavaratti desalination-linked pilot) and wave energy (IIT-M's devices off Tuticorin) — the research frontier where India runs demonstration-scale.

**The synthesis**: conventional supplies **firmness**, non-conventional supplies **growth and cleanliness**; the grid of 2035 pairs them through **storage (PSP/BESS), gas-peaking, demand response and green hydrogen** — 'firm green power' as the destination concept (AP's Pinnapuram the poster project).

Wind power scales with the **cube of wind speed (P ∝ v³)** — micro-siting's physics.
**Floating solar**: Ramagundam (100 MW, NTPC) among India's largest; Omkareshwar expanding.
**2G ethanol refinery: Panipat (2022)** — rice-straw feedstock; **E20 achieved 2025**.
**Geothermal pilot: Puga valley, Ladakh (ONGC)**; hot springs — Manikaran, Tattapani.
**Tidal potential ~12,500 MW** (Khambhat, Kutch, Sundarbans) — unexploited; **OTEC-desalination pilot at Kavaratti (NIOT)**.
Coal generation share ~**75%** despite ~50% non-fossil capacity — the generation-capacity gap.
Bagasse cogeneration and CBG (SATAT) are the bio-workhorses; biomass power ~11 GW.
